title: あまりの～に — so ～ that ～
summary: Shows that something was so extreme that it caused a result: “so ～ that ～.” It attaches to a noun made from an adjective (暑さ, うれしさ), in the form あまりの＋N＋に. The result is an emotion, a reaction or a physical effect.

patterns.form: あまりの ＋ 名詞（〜さ） ＋ に、～
patterns.gloss: あまりの暑さに、～ (because of the extreme heat)

body.p: Change the adjective to a noun with さ (暑い → 暑さ, 忙しい → 忙しさ) and put あまりの in front and に after it. The sentence expresses a strong reaction caused by the extreme degree.
The second half is something that happened as a result, such as めまいがした or 涙が出てきた. It is a fact or reaction, not an order, request or the speaker's intention.

examples.ja: あまりの暑（あつ）さに、めまいがしました。
examples.romaji: Amari no atsusa ni, memai ga shimashita.
examples.tr: I felt dizzy from the extreme heat.

examples.ja: あまりのうれしさに、涙（なみだ）が出（で）てきた。
examples.romaji: Amari no ureshisa ni, namida ga dete kita.
examples.tr: I was so happy that tears started to come out.

examples.ja: あまりの忙（いそが）しさに、昼（ひる）ご飯（はん）を食（た）べるのを忘（わす）れた。
examples.romaji: Amari no isogashisa ni, hirugohan o taberu no o wasureta.
examples.tr: I was so busy that I forgot to eat lunch.

pitfalls: Use a noun with さ after の, not the adjective: あまりの暑さに, not あまりの暑いに.
Do not mix it up with あまり～ない (not very). That is a different pattern.
